name: Nethanel
overview: Nethanel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically for his role as a trumpeter. His identification as a Levite aligns him with the priestly and musical duties assigned to this tribe in Israel. Beyond his musical function, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethanel means 'G-d has given,' reflecting a common theophoric element in Hebrew names that acknowledges divine provision. This meaning is directly tied to the proper name as recorded in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Nethanel as a descendant of Levi, placing him within the Levitical lineage. No other family relationships are documented beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Nethanel's significance in the biblical narrative is connected to his service as a trumpeter among the Levites, a role important for worship and ceremonial functions. His presence in 1 Chronicles 15:24 highlights the organized and divinely appointed structure of temple worship during King David's time. Through his musical contribution, Nethanel participated in the praise of God, reflecting the Levites' dedication to honoring the Lord in the community of Israel.
